text: The evaluation pipeline begins when the dialogue agent's response is received as input.
The response data is routed across four parallel attribute evaluation branches within the combined module.
First, the BERT next sentence prediction branch evaluates the contextual relevance of the response.
In parallel, a dedicated repetition control module measures n-gram overlap across the dialogue.
This submodule computes repetition metrics across internal, external, and partner-level statements.
Third, conversational balance is assessed by counting the number of questions asked.
Fourth, the short-safe attribute monitors utterance length and the presence of named entities.
Each attribute outputs a numeric feature value, forwarding the combined signals into the classification layer.
The classifier integrates all extracted attribute scores to model conversational judgment.
Finally, the module outputs the predicted classification score for conversational fluidity.
